verdict.rationale: Unity documents an official, first-party Unity CLI for installing and managing Editors and modules, aimed at automation and CI. A live probe confirms a keyless install script, structured JSON/TSV output, documented exit codes, an `unity mcp` server mode, and `unity eval` commands built for agents that can run shell commands. Missing for 10: the CLI is still labeled experimental rather than stable, and there is no independent community corroboration of agent use in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Use the Unity CLI to install and manage Unity Editors and modules from the command-line... Use it for new scripts, automation, and CI pipelines.
Unity now ships a first-party standalone CLI (experimental) with a public keyless install script
structured JSON/TSV output and documented exit codes
